items.stem: What is the difference between include and require in PHP?

options.text: require raises a fatal error if the file is missing; include only a warning
options.rationale: require halts execution on failure; include continues with a warning.

options.text: include is for functions and require is for classes
options.rationale: Both just bring in a file; the difference is failure behaviour.
The difference is error handling, not speed.

options.text: They are interchangeable with no difference

items.stem: Select TWO reasons to prefer === over == when comparing values in PHP.

options.text: === compares value and type without type juggling
options.rationale: Strict comparison avoids surprising loose conversions.

options.text: == can treat '0' and false or '' and null as equal in confusing ways
options.rationale: Loose comparison applies type juggling that causes subtle bugs.

items.explanation: Strict comparison avoids surprising loose conversions.

items.stem: Why should form input read from $_POST be validated before use?

options.text: User input is untrusted and may be missing, malformed or malicious
options.rationale: Validation guards against bad or hostile data before it is used.

options.text: Because $_POST is always empty on the first request
options.rationale: Emptiness is only one case; validation covers more.

options.text: Because PHP cannot read POST data otherwise
options.rationale: PHP reads it fine; the issue is trust.

options.text: Because validation converts POST to GET
options.rationale: Validation does not change the HTTP method.

items.explanation: Validation guards against bad or hostile data before it is used.
